strengths: Clear and well-quantified problem motivation: Vision feature extraction bottleneck explicitly identified and measured (83-93% of inference time), making the practical problem compelling

Comprehensive experimental validation: Multiple vision encoders (CLIP, DFN, MetaCLIP, SigLIP2), resolutions, both zero-shot and fine-tuned settings, with thorough ablations on token counts, pool sizes, and training objectives
Significant empirical improvements: 53× inference speedup vs BLIP with competitive retrieval performance; consistent Recall gains across embedding models (up to 15% for CLIP)
Practical modularity: Works as drop-in reranker with different vision encoders and embedding models; well-documented hyperparameters enable reproducibility
Excellent efficiency-performance trade-offs: Achieves 49kB storage per image with 86.9 R@1 on Flickr30k using only 64 compressed tokens
Well-written and clearly presented: Good logical flow of design choices with effective visualizations; principled multi-objective training approach
weaknesses: Comparison fairness concerns: BLIP/BLIP-2 in Table 2 compared under 'cached-vision regime' they weren't designed for; speedup partly from architectural choice rather than compression alone; missing comparison of BLIP/BLIP-2 with precomputed features

Limited conceptual novelty: Offline precomputation established (ColBERT, ColPali); token compression via cross-attention very similar to Q-Former; training objectives are standard approaches; contribution is primarily engineering-focused

Evaluation scope limitations: Only two standard small benchmarks (Flickr30k, COCO); no truly large-scale or web-scale evaluation despite claims; no application-level validation (RAG, content moderation)
Training data mismatch: EDJE trained on 14M samples vs BLIP-2's 400M; limits direct performance comparison fairness; no results with equivalent training data

Insufficient analysis of compression mechanism: No visualization of attention patterns; missing explanation of why token compression preserves performance; no comparison to alternative compression approaches (quantization, pruning)

Negative mining strategy under-analyzed: Relies on embedding model quality with acknowledged false negative risks; sensitivity analysis missing; potential bias toward specific embedding model not addressed
Limited error analysis and failure cases: No discussion of EDJE underperformance scenarios; incomplete robustness evaluation (pool size ablation only on Flickr, not COCO)

Reproducibility uncertainty: Implementation availability stated as conditional ('will be made publicly available shortly'); some implementation details missing (negative mining procedure specifics, precomputation costs)
Unclear downstream task impact: Evaluation limited to Recall@k metrics; no validation that improvements translate to end-task performance in applications like RAG or content filtering

strengths: Clear problem motivation with quantified bottleneck: vision feature extraction consumes 83-93% of inference time in existing joint encoders
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple vision backbones (CLIP, DFN, MetaCLIP, SigLIP2), datasets (Flickr30k, COCO), and retrieval tasks with thorough ablation studies
Practical efficiency gains: ~50× speedup in joint encoding time with storage reduction to 49kB per image, enabling large-scale deployment
Well-written paper with clear presentation of design choices, intuitive figures, and detailed hyperparameters supporting reproducibility
Demonstrates consistent improvements across diverse embedding models, showing modularity as a drop-in reranker
weaknesses: Limited novelty: Core contribution is precomputing features offline (established in ColBERT/ColPali) combined with a simple attention-based adapter similar to existing pooling strategies—incremental rather than novel

Modest performance gains with strong base models: With SigLIP2 (state-of-the-art), R@1 improvements are only 2.2% (ViT-B) and 5.5% (ViT-L); largest gains (~15%) come from weak CLIP baseline, limiting practical impact

Unfair/incomplete comparisons: Table 2's cached-vision regime creates artificial conditions; Table 1's reused vision backbone doesn't isolate EDJE's contribution; missing comparisons with alternative reranking approaches

Unexplained design choices: No ablation justifying MiniLM selection over other compact models; adapter hidden dimension 8192 contradicts 'lightweight' claims; only 3 negatives per sample and k=10 pool size appear conservative without thorough sensitivity analysis

Critical role of distillation underemphasized: Table 5 shows +3.1 R@1 gain from distillation but is relegated to appendix; suggests distillation is essential yet not properly highlighted in main results
Questionable training strategy: In-batch hard negative mining introduces circular dependence on embedding model quality; potential false negatives not quantitatively analyzed
Limited scalability evaluation: Benchmarks are small-scale (Flickr30k: 1k images); no evaluation on truly large candidate sets; throughput claims (50k pairs/sec) lack full specification and context

Reproducibility concerns: Code and checkpoints unavailable at review time ('will be made available shortly'); implementation details for hard negative mining and soft similarity matrix computation underspecified
Narrow ablations: All primary experiments use MiniLM + SigLIP2; limited exploration of language model and vision encoder combinations; token compression guidance for new datasets missing
No evaluation of multilingual or other modalities; limited analysis of failure cases; unclear when/why joint reranking provides benefits beyond ensemble effects

strengths: Clear problem identification with quantified bottleneck analysis (83-93% of inference time spent on vision feature extraction)
Comprehensive empirical evaluation across multiple vision backbones (CLIP, DFN, MetaCLIP, SigLIP2) and benchmarks (Flickr30k, COCO)
Substantial practical efficiency gains (53× speedup) with competitive retrieval performance and modest storage requirements (49kB per image)
Modular design enabling compatibility with any ViT-based vision encoder and pre-trained language model
Thorough ablation studies on token compression, pool size, and training objectives demonstrating robustness
Excellent presentation with clear motivation, logical flow, and informative figures
Good reproducibility with comprehensive hyperparameters and promise to release code
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: combines existing techniques (precomputed features, adapters, attention pooling) without significant innovation; connection to Q-Former insufficiently explored

Fairness concerns in baseline comparisons: assumes precomputed features for all methods in Table 2, but BLIP/BLIP-2 optimized for online inference; large data imbalance (12M vs 400M training examples) confounds results
Narrow evaluation scope: only evaluated in two-stage retrieval pipeline; no end-to-end or standalone system evaluation; missing comparisons with other efficient retrieval/reranking methods
Shallow analysis of token compression: no visualization of what query tokens attend to; no analysis of compression robustness; significant performance drop from 128→64 tokens under-explored
Hard negative mining strategy concerns: reliance on embedding model similarity could introduce circular dependency; 'occasional false negatives' mentioned but not quantified or analyzed
Missing critical practical analysis: disk I/O overhead not discussed; throughput claim (50k pairs/second) needs clarification; storage scaling to billions of images not addressed
Limited generalization analysis: only MiniLM tested; sensitivity to embedding model choice for mining not explored; no cross-dataset or out-of-distribution evaluation
Modest storage requirements still substantial at scale (49TB for 1B images); comparison to uncompressed RGB images is somewhat unfair given efficient image codecs
Potential limited long-term impact as research community shifts toward end-to-end learning and generative approaches, reducing relevance of two-stage retrieval

strengths: Clear identification of a practical bottleneck: vision feature extraction consuming 83-93% of inference time in existing joint encoders, with compelling comparison to text re-rankers
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple vision backbones (CLIP, DFN, MetaCLIP, SigLIP2), resolutions, and realistic settings (including full-dataset retrieval)
Strong empirical results: 53× faster inference than BLIP-2 (1.91ms vs 98.64ms), competitive retrieval performance on Flickr30k, and practical storage footprint (49kB compressed, 442kB uncompressed)
Thorough ablation studies on token compression, pool size, training objectives, negative mining, and quantization, demonstrating robustness and well-understood design choices
Insightful analysis showing compressed tokens preserve semantic structure and alignment, with evidence that full ViT sequence contains substantial redundancy for retrieval
Modular design working as drop-in re-ranker for various embedding models, with practical deployment guidance including pseudocode and I/O analysis
Well-written paper with honest discussion of limitations and comprehensive appendices providing additional experiments and implementation details
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: precomputing vision features offline is well-established (ColBERT, ColPali), cross-attention compression resembles BLIP-2's Q-Former, and contribution primarily combines existing techniques in straightforward manner

Experimental fairness concerns: EDJE trained on smaller dataset (12M images) than BLIP, making direct comparison difficult to interpret; performance gaps on COCO fine-tuned (64.6% vs 66.3%) may reflect data/capacity differences rather than method quality
Missing comparisons with relevant baselines: no comparison with distilled BLIP-2, other efficient re-ranking methods, quantized variants, or finetuned CLIP baselines

Training sensitivity inadequately addressed: hard-negative mining depends on embedding model quality (Section E shows substantial degradation with mismatched models), and other hyperparameter choices (adapter hidden dim, masking rate) lack justification

Evaluation scope limitations: restricted to image-text retrieval without exploring other discriminative tasks (zero-shot classification, VQA); full-dataset evaluation uses different pool size (k=100 vs k=10) limiting comparability

Reproducibility gaps: code not publicly available at review time, some implementation details missing (variable-resolution handling, exact preprocessing), and hyperparameter choices lack thorough justification
Scope limitations: focused on standard English benchmarks without multilingual evaluation or real-world deployment metrics; scaling behavior to web-scale scenarios (billions of images) unexplored

strengths: Clear identification of a genuine practical bottleneck in joint encoder inference (83-93% time in vision feature extraction)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with extensive ablations, multiple vision backbones, and interpretability analysis
Strong efficiency gains: 53× inference speedup and 36-50× storage reduction compared to prior joint encoders
Modular design enabling integration with diverse vision encoders and language models
Publicly available code and detailed deployment guidance enhancing reproducibility and practical utility
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: offline precomputation (ColBERT, ColPali, LightningDOT), attention-based pooling (Q-Former), and token compression are all established; contribution is mainly their straightforward integration

Modest empirical improvements: marginal gains over SigLIP2 embedding model (2-5 R@1 points); no accuracy improvements vs. joint encoders with precomputed features (Table 2: local variant matches BLIP-2)
Evaluation design concerns: fixed small pool size (k=10), training data mismatch (12M vs. BLIP's 129M-400M), missing comparisons with recent joint encoders and simpler baselines
Hard negative mining introduces underdocumented dependencies: Section E shows CLIP miners severely degrade SigLIP2-based EDJE (R@1: 87.8→81.5), limiting generality
Knowledge distillation adds complexity without clear justification: 3 R@1 points come from distillation (Table 5), making it difficult to isolate compression's contribution

Deployment realism oversimplified: I/O costs dismissed as 'same order as compute' but can be substantial at scale; networked storage (common in cloud) explicitly unsupported, limiting practical applicability
Shallow analysis of compression-performance tradeoffs: what spatial/visual details are lost? Why 64 tokens specifically? Cross-modal alignment study is post-hoc, not integrated into training
Limited scope: single task (image-text retrieval), standard benchmarks only; multilingual/video/specialized domains unaddressed despite mention

strengths: Well-motivated problem: Identifies critical bottleneck (83-93% inference time spent on vision encoding) that prevents practical deployment of joint encoders at scale
Elegant and practical solution: Offline precomputation + lightweight attention-based compression adapter + small language model is simple yet effective, easily integrated into existing pipelines

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple backbones (CLIP, DFN, MetaCLIP, SigLIP2) across Flickr30k and COCO, zero-shot and fine-tuned settings, with challenging full-dataset scenarios (Section F)
Substantial empirical results: Achieves 87.8 R@1 on Flickr (competitive with BLIP-2) with 35× faster inference, 5× smaller storage (49kB per image with compression), and 50k pairs/second throughput

Thorough ablations and analysis: Token count trade-offs (Fig 4), pool size robustness (Fig 5), training objectives (Tables 4-5), alternative compression methods (Section G), quantization (Section H), cross-model mining sensitivity (Appendix E)
Strong interpretability analysis: Demonstrates compressed tokens preserve semantic information through nearest-neighbor analysis and quantitative image-caption alignment (Appendices D-D.2)
Practical implementation details: Provides pseudocode, I/O cost analysis, hyperparameters, deployment considerations—enables reproducibility and real-world usage
Excellent presentation: Clear motivation with compelling figures (especially Figure 1), logical organization, detailed appendices, good writing quality
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Combines established techniques (feature precomputation from ColBERT/ColPali, attention-based pooling similar to Q-Formers, lightweight language models) rather than introducing fundamentally new methods
Small-scale training: Uses 12M images versus BLIP-2's 400M; unclear if efficiency advantages and performance gains hold at larger scales; limits confidence in web-scale applicability claims
Narrow evaluation scope: Restricted to image-text retrieval; no evaluation on other discriminative tasks (VQA, classification, grounding); only two main datasets (Flickr30k, COCO)

Incomplete scalability validation: 50k pairs/second throughput includes rough I/O estimates; no experiments at true web-scale; Section C.1 identifies networked storage limitations without solutions; 49kB × billions still substantial

Limited baseline comparisons: Missing comparisons to simpler alternatives (e.g., re-ranking with smaller CLIP models); comparisons primarily to older BLIP/BLIP-2 (2021-2023); no ablation isolating joint modeling gains from architecture choices

Negative mining sensitivity: Appendix E shows catastrophic performance degradation when using SigLIP2→CLIP cross-model mining, suggesting fragility to embedding model choice; deployment implications unclear

Modest novelty in token compression: Cross-attention followed by MLP (Eq. 1-4) is straightforward; very similar to existing attention pooling; alternative simpler methods only compared in appendix (Section G)

Brief discussion of limitations: Section 6 doesn't thoroughly explore failure modes, when offline precomputation loses information, domain shift issues, or which query types benefit most from re-ranking

Reproducibility gap: Code availability promised but not provided with submission; somewhat dated training data sources (CC12M, CC3M, SBU); single language model choice (MiniLM-L12) not well justified against alternatives
